summary: A brick dwelling-and-tower light at Put-in-Bay, lit in 1897 with a fourth-order lens, automated in 1962, and held by Ohio State University since 1967 (permanently since 1997), with summer tours.

lens.where: Lake Erie Islands Historical Society Museum, Put-in-Bay (LighthouseFriends)

structures.note: Tower attached to the brick dwelling; 40 ft base to lantern centre (USLHS). LighthouseFriends gives 45 ft.
Two-and-a-half-story Queen Anne redbrick keeper's dwelling (USLHS)

access.note: Owned by Ohio State University; grounds normally restricted. Summer tours run by the university's Ohio Sea Grant program (2026: Fridays and Saturdays, 12 June to 15 August, 11 a.m. to 4 p.m., free).

visit.note: Visitors climb the stairs to the top of the tower on the university's tours.

facts.agency: Ohio State University (guardian from October 1967 under a thirty-year quitclaim; permanent owner from 1997). Coast Guard still owns the skeletal light tower.

events.note: Congress appropriates $8,600 for the light by the act approved 18 August 1894
About two acres at the southwest point bought from the Parker family for $1,000 (LighthouseFriends)
Contract for a brick dwelling, tower and woodshed being let; first bidder failed to post bond; hired labor completed the work (LighthouseFriends)
Lit for the first time on 10 July 1897 by Keeper Harry H. Riley
Fourth-order L. Sautter & Cie. Fresnel lens; fixed red light through a ruby chimney
Keeper Duggan helps a crew of eight from the burning steam barge Isabel Joyce land at the station and cares for them (LighthouseFriends only)
Changed at the opening of navigation to alternating red and white flashes (LighthouseFriends)
Electric illuminant installed 7 September 1929; white flash raised from 1,800 to 32,000 candlepower, red from 540 to 9,600 (LighthouseFriends)
Automated 26 September 1962; the Coast Guard replaced the lighthouse with an automated light on a steel tower
Coast Guard turns the property over to the federal surplus property division; Ohio State University becomes guardian in October 1967 under a thirty-year quitclaim deed
NOAA meteorological station built on the site (about $50,000)
Ohio State University gains permanent ownership when the quitclaim expires; Coast Guard keeps the skeletal light tower

keepers.name: Harry H. Riley
keepers.note: Lit the light first on 10 July 1897. Taken into custody by Sandusky police 1 September 1898 for problems LighthouseFriends attributes to mental health; died at a state hospital March 1899 (LighthouseFriends only)

keepers.name: Mary Riley
keepers.note: Listed as principal keeper on the roster; LighthouseFriends says she took charge of the light during her husband's illness

keepers.name: Orlo J. Mason
keepers.note: Called Colonel Orlo J. Mason by LighthouseFriends

keepers.name: Charles B. Duggan
keepers.note: Came from five years at West Sister Island; cultivated twenty acres; died after a fall from a 45-ft cliff in April 1925 (LighthouseFriends; putinbay.com). Named in the Commissioner's fiscal 1915 list.

keepers.name: Lyle C. Duggan
keepers.note: Twenty-year-old son; cared for the light after his father's death until the next year (LighthouseFriends)

keepers.name: William L. Gordon
keepers.note: Transferred from Green Island in 1926. LighthouseFriends gives William F. Gordon; the roster gives William L.

keepers.name: Frank LaRose
keepers.note: Digital Archive record: retired from here, 1941 (the record's source is the National Archive Retirement Cards). The Digital Archive person record lists the old Fairport Harbor light as principal for 1927-1937, the same years as the breakwater post.

keepers.name: Paul F. Prochnow
keepers.note: Last keeper; light automated 26 September 1962. LighthouseFriends counts fifteen years at the station.

wrecks.outcome: Crew of eight landed at the station by Keeper Charles B. Duggan and cared for there (LighthouseFriends only)

corrections.proposed: tower, brick, built 1897, 12.2 m (40 ft base to lantern centre), standing
corrections.why: The Digital Archive gives the tower as established 1897; LighthouseFriends gives 1897 for the first light; the Board's 1896 report shows the buildings still being contracted in that year. 1895 is the land purchase. The record's 21.0 m does not match 40 ft (USLHS) or 45 ft (LighthouseFriends).
USLHS gives the height of the light above water as 60.5 ft (about 18.4 m). Check against the Light List before adopting; a discontinued light has no current Light List entry.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1895 'built' is the year the land was bought. The appropriation came on 18 August 1894, the building contract was let in fiscal 1896, and the light was first lit on 10 July 1897, the year the tower is established in the USLHS record.

notes_for_editor:
Sources. The NRHP nomination (NRIS 90000473) is a 22 KB 'not yet digitized' placeholder; the story uses only the NPGallery metadata (architect, listing date). The Chronicling America search for 'Isabel Joyce' and 'Put-in-Bay' in 1915 returned no pages (after one retry on an HTTP 520), so the Isabel Joyce rescue, Riley's 1898 custody and 1899 death, and Duggan's 1925 fall all rest on LighthouseFriends and putinbay.com alone. The 1891 and 1895 Board passages are the report's own text.

OCR matching. The Commissioner's fiscal 1915 list (scan 68) prints 'C. Duggan, keeper, S. Bass Island Light Station, Ohio' in a column of names; the vessels aided are in a separate column that the OCR does not keep aligned, so the Isabel Joyce link is not confirmed from that list. The page image was not read; the OCR does not pair Duggan's name with a vessel, and the story does not claim that pairing. The name was matched as printed, not by column position.

Names. The roster says William L. Gordon and LighthouseFriends says William F. Gordon. The story gives the roster's name and notes the difference. The Digital Archive's 'Frank LaRose' person page links his Fairport Harbor, Fairport Harbor West Breakwater and South Bass Island posts; the other_stations entries rest on that page.

Record checks. The record's characteristic (Fl R 6s) matches neither the 1897 fixed red nor the alternating red and white flashes from 1926 that LighthouseFriends describes; it is not in facts. The record's range (10.4 nm) was not verified. Corrections for the tower height and the focal height are proposed, not applied.

Privacy. Prochnow's personal incident (a car through the ice in 1959, in LighthouseFriends) is left out, as are the private details of the 1898 incident beyond what is needed. The 2026 tour notice on a Stone Lab social post is not cited; the Ohio Sea Grant page is.

Tours. The Ohio Sea Grant page lists 2026 tours from 12 June to 15 August, which is over as of 2026-10-22.
